main_body: Flat ground patch of dark grey-brown cobble/scale paving tiled across the 4x3 tile area; no standing volume.
top_band: none (terrain surface, repeating cobble pattern with lighter cobble tops and dark gaps)
evidence: The candidate is a seamless ground/paving texture, not a standing object. The 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply to terrain tiles. No side faces are drawn and it reads as a flat repeating floor pattern, so there is no 3/4 failure.

style.evidence: The reference paving has individually shaded stones with highlight edges, grain and varied slab layout. The candidate is a monotone repeating scale/cobble motif with about 4 lightness steps (near-black gaps, dark, mid, light highlight caps). The gaps are tinted dark grey-brown rather than pure black. There is some per-stone variation, but the motif repeats on a rigid grid with identical highlights every row, so it looks mechanical and lower in variety than the reference. Most areas are 2-3 close dark tones and larger regions are dark mid-tone fills with little grain. Density per tile is lower than the reference, and the pattern is too uniform and low-contrast to sit next to it without looking thinner.
